videos.script: The shop now has more than one network. Production, staging, and a copy in Virginia for a bad day. {{three}} This lesson joins them, in two ways. {{peering}} A peering connection joins exactly two VPCs. It costs nothing by the hour, and it has three rules. The ranges must not overlap. Both sides need a route. And nothing passes through. {{transitive}} If production is peered with staging and with the copy, staging still cannot reach the copy. {{hub}} A Transit Gateway is the other way. It is a hub. Each network attaches once, and the hub's own route tables decide who reaches whom. {{tables}} That can say things peering cannot, such as staging and production both reaching shared tools, but never each other. {{price}} The hub is charged for every attachment, every hour, and for every gigabyte it carries. So you will price both, for two VPCs and for ten. {{end}} By the end you can say which one the shop should use today, and on what day it should change.
